chapter: Defining R&B and the New Orleans sound
title: Whether R&B should have been called rhythm and gospel
summary: Jones relays a Jerry Wexler remark; King talks about gospel roots and soul expression.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I'm going to quote this to one person, when we started to define R&B, and I think there's another element that we touched on earlier, and a friend of yours, Jerry Marksler, who was president, vice president of Atlantic Records, who produced a number of R&B records in the 50s. One said that maybe it shouldn't have been called R&B, maybe it should have been called Rhythm and Gospel, instead of Rhythm and Blues. What do you think?

I think it probably would have took on a bad thing, because the Gospel, the people in the Gospel thing, was a problem, it was like they were priming on Great Charles, and a lot of things that, you know, on the borderline of some sense of the Gospel.
I think what he meant is that there was so much Gospel influence in people.
Yeah, I could understand, and it probably would have been meaningful, but some people would have taken it the wrong way, you know. Because of the attitude.

I think what he was saying is that, like yourself, many of the R&B artists who sang, or wrote, came from a church background. All of them started in church singing, and then took their talents, and their knowledge, and what they gave them to church, and then went to the studio and recorded. Yeah.

Well, I look at that twofold, because some of the people that really started in the church, I think Gospel music gave the individual a chance to reach out at what we call today, at the peak level of soul expression, as they used nowadays. So, and I think in the music loop, and you say this also, because many of the major recording companies used to come in, and this is the first thing you'd be singing something, and it's a, hey, stop. Like, you're not putting enough into it, you're just going to have enough for this other thing. You've got to put some soul. And I think Jerry Wicksburg might have instituted that. You know, he may have, he could have been the person that instituted that at the time. The word may have, you know, around loosely. I'm not sure, but I think he did.
